packages.summary: Rigid mesh clusters, static scenery HLOD, CPU occlusion and offline baked surface proxies
packages.notes: Use geometry_catalog/analyze before setting explicit policies. Ordinary instancing remains for crowds. HLOD is static scenery only, not gameplay or fog visibility. Verify real cameras and hardware; no virtual geometry streaming or GPU Hi-Z.

packages.summary: Fixed arithmetic, trigonometry, interpolation, rotations, matrices, curves and numerical solvers
packages.notes: Engine reference; Q16 bounded algorithms, no new verification.

packages.summary: FIFO queue and stable top-K
packages.notes: Store queue under NativeState. top ties preserve input order; sort entity inputs by index.

packages.summary: Graph traversal, weighted paths, connectivity, spanning forests and integral flows
packages.notes: Integer graph algorithms; signed paths flag negative cycles; flow budgets and restrictions documented in skill. No new verification.

packages.summary: Generic spatial grids, hashes, BVH and trees
packages.notes: Use common algorithms for new code; existing GameCore queries remain compatibility adapters pending migration. Integer AABB; floating distance queries not lockstep guaranteed.

packages.summary: 2D/3D grid traversal, components, morphology, distance fields and seeded watershed
packages.notes: Use row-major IDs. Zero cells are blocked. Bound work and cache under NativeState. Test borders and unreachable cells.

packages.summary: Existing pathfinding, navigation mesh and flow fields
packages.notes: Reuse movement commands; do not move entities from view scripts. Grid A*/HPA* by default; movement.pathfinding navmesh uses the engine/nav mesh on flat maps (docs/navmesh.md). Test blocked goals, arrival and planets separately.

packages.summary: FSM transitions and utility selection
packages.notes: Persist current state explicitly. Definitions are immutable. Utility ties choose smaller ID. BT/GOAP remain planned.

packages.summary: Priority task claiming and worker release
packages.notes: Use unique task IDs and numeric priority. Set status pending initially. Release dead workers; validate ownership before finishing. Dependencies remain planned.

packages.summary: Atomic integer recipe consumption
packages.notes: Use resource indices and nonnegative integer amounts. Duplicate ingredients are summed. This operates on caller stock, not engine resources; never create a competing economy.

packages.summary: Ordered all/any predicates
packages.notes: Keep functions in immutable definitions, never persistent NativeState. Empty all is true; empty any false. Formula parser remains planned.

packages.summary: Weighted selection and level thresholds
packages.notes: Supply simulation RNG as draw(total), integer 1..total. Zero total returns nullopt. Test zero weights and endpoints. Pity systems remain planned.

packages.summary: Event counters and one-shot completion
packages.notes: Use unique goal IDs and positive integer targets. Save progress. Emit completion only on threshold crossing. Branching dialogue remains planned.

packages.summary: Existing deterministic map generator
packages.notes: Reuse generation presets and engine seeds. Validate fair starts and connectivity. New Poisson/WFC adapters remain planned.

packages.summary: Smoothstep, lerp and timeline progress
packages.notes: Use presentation C++ only. Zero duration completes at start. Read sim events and never write simulation NativeState.

packages.summary: Existing UI templates
packages.notes: Reuse RmlUi templates and localization. Send commands through documented bindings. Virtualized list package remains planned.

packages.summary: Existing snapshot restoration verification
packages.notes: Run tests and sample matches for sim changes. Restore verification does not prove cross-platform determinism. Profile separately from verification.

packages.summary: AIVerse InputFlow: typed Input Actions, mapping contexts, modifiers, triggers, local multiplayer, user profiles and legacy Input.h compatibility
packages.notes: AIVerse InputFlow canonical API: engine/platform/input/InputFlowCore.h, aiverse::lib::gameplay::inputflow::InputFlow; platform facade engine/platform/InputFlow.h. Keep EnhancedInput.h and enhanced::InputSystem as compatibility aliases. Use AIVERSE::InputFlow (or AIVERSE::lib_inputflow); legacy AIVERSE::lib_input remains stable. Presentation-only: gameplay consumes validated Commands. See docs/enhanced-input.md and the agent handoff.

packages.summary: Ground camera pose limits and exponential easing (target, zoom, yaw, pitch); the engine follow camera runs on it
packages.notes: Use delta time only in presentation. Apply resulting Pose to the existing client/editor camera. World-to-sphere mapping remains the planet camera responsibility.

packages.summary: Construction grids, placement checks, resource explanations, refunds and native construction commands
packages.notes: Call checkPlacement with authoritative map/territory/slope queries. Render its Decision as preview, then submit buildCommand. The engine must revalidate the command at execution time; previews never reserve or debit resources.

packages.summary: Target/range/resource checks and optional native cast/cooldown lifecycle
packages.notes: For built-in abilities send abilityCommand and use engine cooldown/effects. Use AbilityState only for custom native mechanics, and persist all fields. Charge custom resource costs transactionally only after validation.

packages.summary: Stacked inventory, weight/slot limits, atomic transfer, equipment and crafting
packages.notes: Prefer built-in engine item mechanics for existing item types. For custom native inventories validate item definitions, provide stable IDs, serialize each stack/equipment field, and require ownership checks in commands.

packages.summary: Tiered protective gear for any genre: slot pieces (helmet, vest, shield, backpack) that absorb a share of damage to the zones they cover, wear with the absorbed damage, break, add carry capacity, replace each other on equip and compare for automatic pickups
packages.notes: Integer milli-shares, deterministic, bounded. The owner picks the hit zone bit, applies the returned damage and drops the replaced piece as loot with its durability. Persist GearLoadout with io (Archive) and fold gearHash into the checksum. Used by the FPS module (fps.gear). No visuals, no item database or inventory ownership beyond the slots.

packages.summary: Leader election, role ordering, formation slots and native group commands
packages.notes: Use formationCommand for engine formations; use formationSlots for custom planning only. Sort/tie-break by entity ID. Feed desired slots to navigation rather than teleporting units.

packages.summary: Event-to-sound/particle/animation/notification/camera actions with cooldowns
packages.notes: Bind dispatch callbacks to existing presentation services. Use only accepted sim events; clear FeedbackState after rollback/seek and never feed it into gameplay logic.

packages.summary: Event-driven tutorial stages, counters, branches, skip and hard/soft action gating
packages.notes: Validate immutable steps at load. Persist step/progress/complete in NativeState. Hard gating must also validate commands, not only hide UI. Highlight is a host UI target ID, not a renderer.

packages.summary: Transactional versioned state migrations plus checksummed JSON backup tools
packages.notes: Migrate on import/load before installing state. Engine nativeModules VERSION compatibility is distinct: this API cannot force an incompatible engine save to load. Use gameplay.py save/restore for JSON envelopes only.

packages.summary: Structured refusal codes, values and bounded decision traces
packages.notes: Use reasonKey with Localization::tr; pass subject/required/available as parameters. Traces are diagnostic outputs only; never depend on trace capacity for simulation outcomes.

packages.summary: Content budgets, PNG dimensions, localization consistency and existing conversion tool orchestration
packages.notes: Run audit, then pipeline with explicit modelconv/audiopack paths. Conversion capability depends on the engine tool build. Source licensing is still the project author responsibility.

packages.summary: Headless seed checks, snapshot/serialized restore gates and machine-readable reports
packages.notes: Run verify against the built project-specific headless executable. Set requireWinner for combat scenarios; tutorial/sandbox scenarios may intentionally have no winner. A successful headless run does not validate UI rendering.

packages.summary: Plan and validated application of resource/building/ability/faction changes
packages.notes: Generate a plan, inspect checks, then apply with the real project-specific headless executable. Apply validates a staged copy before replacing rules.json and retains a content-addressed backup. Never overwrite a stale plan.

packages.summary: Generated C++ settings, JSON Schema, defaults and strict config parsing
packages.notes: Edit libraries/spec/gameplay.json and regenerate. C++ loader and CLI reject unknown fields, wrong types and cross-field violations. Do not edit generated files by hand.

packages.summary: Snapshot UI bindings, escaped values and bounded action queues
packages.notes: Use BindingModel.set/drain on a read-only snapshot. Invalidate after document reload or language change. Dispatch Actions through host Command routing. Do not retain simulation references.

packages.summary: Configurable screen rows, modal routing and RmlUi binding
packages.notes: Use Screen/ScreenStack and the RmlScreenBinding adapter. Supply rows for HUD, building, units, inventory, technology, pause and results. Destroy bindings before document roots. Revalidate action ownership and affordability in the sim. Rendering needs host integration and screenshot QA.

packages.summary: Safe-area layouts, density clamp and validated theme tokens
packages.notes: Use layout with framebuffer or dp units consistently; never mix them. Apply safe insets from the platform. themeStyles emits RmlUi RCSS dp units. Resolve translations before markup. Test portrait/landscape and large text.

packages.summary: Authoritative match result to idempotent meta transaction
packages.notes: Use grantMatch with aiverse::meta::Economy after authoritative completion. Link aiverse::meta and provide durable Commit CAS. Keep a stable unique match id across retries. Never call from predicted finishes, replay seeks or sim ticks. Nullopt is invalid envelope; inspect meta Result for conflict/denial.

packages.summary: Application state transitions and stale loading completion rejection
packages.notes: Use Lifecycle.send for explicit events. Capture generation before async load and call loaded(ticket). Host owns cancellation and resource cleanup. Pausing local UI must not stop a shared multiplayer simulation.

packages.summary: Transport-independent lobby, reconnect and ordered delivery policy
packages.notes: Provide transport/authentication outside this package. Use epoch on each async callback; retain sequence across reconnect and reset on a new session. Content hashes must come from verified manifests. accept is for ordered message streams, not out-of-order UDP or multiple peer channels. Do not present this as a server or netcode implementation.

packages.summary: Versioned dependency resolution, conflicts and deterministic mod order
packages.notes: Build ContentPackage records from trusted manifests, then resolveContent. Digest is required metadata, not computed or verified here; verify actual bytes through catalog pins/content tooling before mounting. Mount in returned order with explicit override rules. Never execute untrusted scripts or use manifest paths without validation.

packages.summary: Mirrored round-robin cases and aggregate faction outcomes
packages.notes: Use roundRobin with identical seed lists and swapped starts. Record actual player-to-faction mapping. Use addSample only for completed matches/draws; keep time limits separate. Run playlab.py against prepared project variations; report sample counts and seeds, not unsupported confidence claims.

packages.summary: Tick-indexed actions and assertions for automated play
packages.notes: Validate Scenario once before running. Advance at every exact tick; emit normal Commands via callback and supply authoritative metric snapshots. Missing metrics and skipped ticks fail. Reset the runner for each run; do not reuse it after rollback without restoring cursor state.

packages.summary: Nearest-rank p95, peak limits and baseline regression checks
packages.notes: Collect timing outside sim after warm-up on the same hardware/build/quality. Samples and budgets must share units. Use summarize and checkBudget; insufficient samples fail. Never let timing metrics affect deterministic gameplay. Report peak and sample count as well as p95.

packages.summary: Reusable capability and acceptance recipes for sixteen genres
packages.notes: Use genreKit to select existing library packages and acceptance scenarios. Configure engine rules and templates before adding code. Kits are composition recipes, not complete generated games. Implement the named acceptance scenarios for the actual project and verify them.

packages.summary: Dependency-ordered change recipes and verification checklist
packages.notes: Describe explicit ChangeRecipe dependencies/files/checks and call planChanges. Unknown IDs and cycles fail. Review actual file diffs; the planner does not infer semantics or edit files. Apply supported rule mutations with existing gameplay.py recipe/apply and its stale-base checks.

packages.summary: Generate a registered external native C++ module
packages.notes: Generate into a new directory from a reviewed schema. Never overwrite custom module handlers; review the generated diff. Merge rules.fragment.json into nativeModules explicitly. Run the generated Smoke.cpp and external-native tests. Module.cpp intentionally has no game-specific effects.

packages.summary: Generate typed NativeState access and transactional migrations
packages.notes: Declare bounded int64 and bool fields. Use initialize only for empty setup state; load validates schema/ranges, store validates atomically. Define explicit rename/set/erase migration steps. Migration does not bypass engine nativeModules VERSION compatibility. Keep engine simulation state in NativeState.

packages.summary: Generate typed native Command encoders and dispatch
packages.notes: Reserve a project-unique commandType in 32768..65535 and unique action IDs. Use encode then Simulation.submit. decode checks type, action, nonneutral player, exact argument count and bounds. Handlers must separately validate player range, ownership, resources and target lifetimes. Commands do not grant authority.

packages.summary: Validate ID, file and localization/content references
packages.notes: Supply explicit source/target selectors. Use /@keys for dictionaries and /* for arrays/objects. Configure required matches for mandatory categories; optional zero matches are allowed. Use the shipped rules preset, then add schema-specific ability/audio/localization selectors. Run the real engine validator too; this is not a full rules parser.

packages.summary: Stage and atomically activate validated host settings
packages.notes: Stage with parser returning optional settings and a validator. Commit only at a safe point using expected revision. Failed staging clears pending data and preserves live settings. Handle parser exceptions in the host. Never hot-reload deterministic gameplay state using a filesystem clock; replicate gameplay changes through Commands.

packages.summary: Fixed-capacity scratch buffers and generational slot pools
packages.notes: Choose capacity from a documented budget; handle full buffers/pools explicitly. Stale or released handles fail. Slot indices are allocated in deterministic order. Capacity bounds objects, not heap memory inside T. Use fixed-size element types in hot paths. Persist pool/handle state through NativeState if it affects outcomes.

packages.summary: Deterministic round-robin work with operation budgets
packages.notes: Keep WorkItems sorted by unique ID. Each callback performs one bounded operation without modifying the items span or cursor. Persist completed counters and WorkCursor for rollback. Failed callback must leave its own output untouched. Never budget by elapsed wall time or use unordered iteration.

packages.summary: Locate the first differing native field and trace tick
packages.notes: Use firstStateDifference for NativeState-compatible maps and arrays. Export canonical tick/modules snapshots from both runs, then use project_checks.py desync. Missing or differently sampled ticks are coverage errors. Only exported fields can be diagnosed; this does not automatically instrument every ECS pool.

packages.summary: Read-only package upgrade plan from lock hashes
packages.notes: Compare schema-2 libraries.lock.json with the current catalog/engine root. Review version changes, changed transitive files and required checks. The tool never updates pins or migrates code automatically. Run project tests and update pins only as an explicit reviewed project change.

packages.summary: End-to-end real RTS simulation, RmlUi, save and meta reward example
packages.notes: Create isolated content with showcase_project.py. Build the opt-in aiverse_library_showcase target and run --auto with a fresh output directory. Check actual build/attack events, save checksum round trip, idempotent meta rewards and screenshot. Reward storage is a single-process example, not a production backend. Use distinct match IDs for distinct authoritative matches.

packages.summary: Authoritative effective stat snapshots through existing modifiers
packages.notes: Call effectiveStats after checking the entity. Configure existing StatMod/tech/level/status rules; never evaluate a parallel modifier stack. The snapshot returns final values, not an invented per-source breakdown. Missing units and invalid stats fail.

packages.summary: Status snapshots and validated entry to the existing status engine
packages.notes: Use statuses for copies of active stacks/expiry/source data. applyStatus is a simulation-only hook after authority checks, outside ECS iteration. True means valid invocation, not proof a status bypassed immunity. Engine statuses own refresh, stacks, periods, flags and hashing.

packages.summary: All/any/none tag filters and bounded-value conditions
packages.notes: Resolve type tags using Rules.tagMask; reject unknown names with resolveTags. Keep type tags separate from status/dispel tags. Missing condition inputs fail closed. Built-in EffectDef target filters remain authoritative.

packages.summary: Stable action previews plus native built-in interaction commands
packages.notes: Use interactions for sorted preview options and disabled reasons. Build actual Smart/PickItem/UseItem/Load/ToggleLock Commands with EngineMechanics.interactionCommand, then submit through Simulation. For ToggleLock actor is the selected gate; PickItem uses point. Custom actions use generated native commands and revalidate at execution. Physical carry/throw/push/ropes/doors/platforms/breakables are the separate physical-interactions package; previews here must not authorize those mutations.

packages.summary: Transactional reservation, release and consumption of custom capacities
packages.notes: Use ticket and owner IDs > 0. Repeating an identical live reservation is Duplicate; conflicting payload/owner fails. Commit validates aggregate capacity before changing stock; release does not consume. Keep built-in Inventory.reserved under its existing owner. Persist tickets with Persistence.h; handle cancellation and owner destruction.

packages.summary: Tick-based multi-stage actions with timeout and cancellation cleanup
packages.notes: Advance once per increasing tick. begin false must have no side effects; poll is read-only; cleanup is called once for each entered stage on completion/cancel/failure. One stage transition per call bounds work. Implement navigation through existing commands; persist sequence state. Couple reservations to stage cleanup.

packages.summary: Weighted loot with exclusions and a guaranteed rare threshold
packages.notes: Reuse weighted selection through rollLoot. Draw must return an integer in [1,total]; use rollSimLoot to consume sim.rng with a validated uint32 total. Guarantee N forces eligible rare loot on attempt N after N-1 misses. Impossible guarantees fail without drawing. Persist pity state and validate/exclude before sampling; reward granting remains separate.

packages.summary: Nonnegative integer step/linear progression tables and CLI preview
packages.notes: Author strictly increasing nonnegative x and nonnegative y. Endpoints clamp; linear rounding is toward the left value, including descending segments. Unsafe intermediate products return failure. Use aiverse_app_tools curve to preview exact runtime results; use engine/meta progression owners for built-in experience/rewards.

packages.summary: Bounded observation memory, expiration and threat selection
packages.notes: Feed only visibility-authorized observations; never enumerate hidden enemies into memory. Keep known positions after lost sight until tick TTL expires. Highest threat ties by smaller entity ID; capacity evicts oldest, then smaller ID, and rejects older incoming observations. Use stable packed IDs and clear destroyed targets only when knowledge permits. Persist via Persistence.h.

packages.summary: Bounded structured decision facts using existing reason codes
packages.notes: Collect facts from the actual authoritative calculation, including localization key/subject/required/actual/reason. explain keeps the first failure even when fact output is truncated. Do not infer damage/modifier explanations from guessed formulas. Send display-only reports to UI/debug consumers; keep diagnostics out of state hashes unless they drive behavior.

packages.summary: RTS bot profiles and transactional checkpoints over the existing ComputerPlayer
packages.notes: Use existing ComputerPlayer for economy, build/research, combat, garrisons and terrain/planet play. Host calls update before sim.step. rules.ai may override profiles. Preserve the legacy knowledge policy; do not claim fog-fairness. Save bot state with simulation; exact player/seed/settings must match.

packages.summary: Command-driven FPS bots with perception, reaction, aiming, reload, retreat, zone and patrol
packages.notes: Run on one authoritative host with map bot:false for owned slots. Use fpsCommand then sim.submit; never mutate character components. Persist FpsState with the simulation. Supply generated navmesh or authored waypoint graph; no bomb, loot or vehicle mechanics are implied. 0.1.4: with fps.royale the zone goal is the announced battle-royale circle (Module::royaleView); FPS rules fps.bots host this controller inside the module for map bots (docs/fps.md § Library bots).

packages.summary: Automatic deterministic layered AABB navigation mesh with clearance, erosion and any-angle routing on the engine navmesh
packages.notes: FPS adapter over the genre-independent engine/nav mesh (docs/navmesh.md): collision spans merge into rectangles, A* + funnel give any-angle routes. Build immutable regional meshes from current collision and motor dimensions. Rebuild on geometry changes. Bound cell/polygon/candidate/search budgets. No triangle/slope importer or cross-region streaming links. Use navPath/navStep, real motor tests and aiverse_navmesh exporter.

packages.summary: Procedural enterable buildings from axis-aligned boxes: 1..10 floors, slabs, outer walls with a seeded door side and windows, interior partition with a doorway, switchback stairwell with slab holes, roof, loot spots, door points; quarter-turn yaw; validated against the agent size and step height; stair halls (nav goals beside each flight end)
packages.notes: Fixed math, deterministic per definition + seed. Output boxes go into the owner's static collision (FPS map `buildings`, AABB navmesh, cover maps). Agent radius / height / max step rise come from the owner's motor; generateBuilding returns nullopt when the doorway, stairwell or windows do not fit. No meshes, materials, rotated walls or furniture.

packages.summary: Actual RTS/FPS bot matches, decision counters and restoration regression tests
packages.notes: Build aiverse_bot_match and root library bot/navmesh tests. Example FPS navmesh bounds target arena; author region bounds for other maps. A timeout is not a win, and bot difficulty presets are not an Elo claim.

packages.summary: Fixed character movement policy: ground/air acceleration, jump buffer, coyote time, slopes, ledges, ladders, swimming, climbing, mantle/vault, dash, wall slide, wall run, grapple and one-way platform modes
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md for exact coverage and authority boundaries. 0.2.0 adds LocomotionModes.h: a Ground/Air/Ledge/Ladder/Swim/Climb/Mantle state machine driven by owner-reported environment queries (no physics inside), optional locomotion.* settings, versioned/hashable LocomotionState; stepMotion is unchanged. 0.3.0 adds Dash/WallSlide/WallRun/Grapple modes, one-way drop-through with LocomotionResult::ignoreOneWay and oneWaySupports, new locomotion.* settings and state kind 21 (kind 20 still loads; 0.2.0 config/state hashes unchanged at defaults). Policies do not automatically replace existing engine movement/combat/victory or wire presentation. Persist versioned state and bind immutable definitions. Use actual native/host owners for commands, collision and damage.

packages.summary: Custom melee timing, buffered combos, active-window hit deduplication and defense outcomes
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md for exact coverage and authority boundaries. Policies do not automatically replace existing engine movement/combat/victory or wire presentation. Persist versioned state and bind immutable definitions. Use actual native/host owners for commands, collision and damage.

packages.summary: Frame-keyed hitboxes/hurtboxes (sphere/capsule/box), dodge invulnerability, directional guard and perfect parry, poise/stagger and lock-on targeting composed over melee-combat
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (combat-actions) for exact coverage and authority boundaries. Produces contacts and outcomes only: damage, stamina, health and statuses stay with the existing combat owner. Fixed math and integer ticks; repeated/backwards ticks are rejected. Persist CombatActorState via genre::save/load (record kinds 32..36) and hash it with combatHash.

packages.summary: Per-agent stealth perception: sight cones with near/peripheral ranges and owner multipliers, hearing with occlusion and noise budgets, footprint/scent trails, suspicion meters with Unaware/Suspicious/Searching/Alert thresholds, delayed ally alerts with shared last known positions, deterministic search points, disguises and hiding spots
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (stealth-senses) for exact coverage and authority boundaries. Generic per-agent policy, not RTS fog of war (modules/rts vision stays authoritative there). The owner supplies poses, light/cover/stance/visibility multipliers, LOS and occlusion callbacks (called in observer-id then target/noise order under per-tick budgets) and search candidates; outputs are PerceivedTarget records and SenseEvents, never movement. Fixed math, integer ticks, repeated/backwards ticks rejected. Persist SensesState via genre::save/load (record kinds 48..55 reserved, 48..52 used) and hash with sensesHash; bind sensesConfigHash. Optional `senses` settings section.

packages.summary: Authoritative scene flow: integer-ratio time-scale domains (world/player/ui/cinematic) with stacked priority requests, exact accumulators, hit-stop/slow-motion presets; scene timelines of dialogue/animation/camera/sound/event cues with play/pause/skip/seek; sync waits on host-reported line/marker/in-position facts with timeouts; QTE press/mash/hold/sequence judged on input ticks with difficulty and accessibility; interaction staging with marks, teleport fallback and input locks; checkpoint requests and resume at sync points; narrative cue triggers
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (cinematic-gameplay) for the determinism model. Authoritative: time-scale requests/accumulators, timeline position, cue emission (essential cues once per run, presentation cues once per pass), wait/QTE outcomes, staging and input locks. Host: audio/animation/camera playback and navigation, reported back as tick-stamped SceneInput; every wait and staging move has a timeout so devices cannot stall the sim. stepTime/stepScene once per strictly increasing tick; invalid input returns nullopt with state untouched. Narrative CueRequest{cueId} bridges through cueTrigger/sceneForCue. Persist TimeState/SceneState via genre::save/load (record kinds 72..79 reserved, 72..75 used); hash with cinematicHash and bind sceneLibraryHash. Optional `cinematic` settings section. No rendering, audio, animation playback or cutscene editor. genre/NarrativeCinematicBridge.h (queueNarrativeCues/releaseNarrativeCues) schedules narrative-graphs CueRequest records (tick + delayTicks, deduped by sequence) into TriggerCue scene commands; its NarrativeCueQueue is record kind 76.

packages.summary: MotionWeave presentation animation for any project: graph player, blend trees, IK, motion matching, sectioned montages with slots and bone masks, clip notifies, root motion extraction and baking with a fixed-point motor adapter, motion warping, humanoid and generic retargeting, pose inertialization, crowd budgets and jobs, facial control rig, optional Box3D ragdoll bridge
packages.notes: Headers live in libraries/include/aiverselib/animation/ (AnimationMontage.h, AnimationPlayback.h, EcsRootMotionSystems.h, RootMotionBaker.h, AnimationMotionWarp.h, HumanoidRetarget.h, GenericRetarget.h, PoseInertialization.h, AnimationCrowdSystems.h, FacialControlRig.h, PhysicsRagdollBridge.h). Presentation World only: never put float graph state or poses in Simulation::world(); authoritative root motion goes through the fixed-point motor adapter. Legacy target AIVERSE::animation_ecs stays valid; ragdoll needs AIVERSE_ENABLE_PHYSICS=ON (AIVERSE::animation_physics). Tests: tests/animation. Not done: audio-driven lip-sync, live game-scene/prefab binding, HTML5 Studio viewport. Read docs/motionweave.md.

packages.summary: Card and board game rules: data-defined cards (units/spells/instants with targets and ordered effects: damage, heal, draw, energy, buff, counter, reveal, mill) and rule variants (hand/health/energy curve, draw per turn, first-player skip, fatigue, overdraw burn, board limit, turn limit, separate combat phase, rush, partial/full mulligan); seeded deck shuffles, draw/mulligan, phases, legal action generation, LIFO effect stack with priority passing, counters and fizzling on invalid targets, guard attacks, per-seat hidden information with a non-leaking cardViewFor projection and redacted/reveal events
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (Cards and turn strategy) for exact coverage. Composes card-runtime's zone vocabulary (cardRuntimeZone) and leaves strategy/Cards.h unchanged. cardGameSetup/stepCardGame are the only mutation path: strictly increasing command seq, seat holding priority, action in cardLegalActions (computed from the seat's own view); invalid input returns nullopt with state and RNG untouched; RNG (passed-in aiverse::Random) only for setup/mulligan shuffles. Send seats only cardViewFor/cardEventsFor; lockstep replication is not confidential. Persist CardGameState via genre::save/load (record kind 96; 96..103 reserved for cards+turns), hash with cardGameHash, bind cardLibraryHash. JSON via readCardLibrary/readCardDecks with path-qualified errors; optional cardGame settings section. No deck builder, trigger/replacement language, collection or transport.

packages.summary: Turn strategy on square/hex grids: weighted 8-way/hex movement with deterministic reachable sets and paths, half/full cover from the owner grid with a flank angle, integer line of fire and shot previews (hit chance milli), action points, per-round initiative with speed modifiers and stable-id ties, delay, overwatch reservations firing reaction shots, per-team visibility projection, and WeGo simultaneous resolution (collected orders, lockstep movement with contested-cell/swap rules, simultaneous fire)
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (Cards and turn strategy) for exact coverage. turn-scheduler (strategy/Turns.h, fixed order + nested LIFO reactions) is unchanged and remains the choice for host-applied effects; tactics-grid owns a dynamic order. stepTactics / tacticsResolveWeGo: strictly increasing seq, active unit only, action in tacticsLegalActions; invalid input returns nullopt with state untouched; one RNG draw per shot from the passed-in aiverse::Random. Send teams only tacticsViewFor/tacticsEventsFor. Persist TacticsState (98) and TacticsOrders (99) via genre::save/load; hash with tacticsHash, bind tacticsScenarioHash. JSON via readTacticsScenario with path-qualified errors; optional tactics settings section. Units never block line of fire; no elevation, destructible cover, campaign or animation.

packages.summary: Deterministic turn and card bots that see only their own view: a tactics turn planner scoring reachable destinations, attacks and overwatch (expected damage, kill chance, seen threats, cover, objective advance) under a bounded search budget, and a card evaluator scoring legal actions with real-rules simulation on a view-rebuilt state and bounded lookahead
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (Cards and turn strategy). Bots return player-equivalent CardAction/TacticsAction for stepCardGame/stepTactics and never write state; inputs are cardViewFor/tacticsViewFor only (hidden cards and unseen units cannot change a choice, tested). No RNG; stateless (nothing to persist). Budgets: cardGame.botNodeBudget/botDepth and tactics.botSearchBudget settings.

packages.summary: Seeded spread, recoil, swept projectiles with ricochets, material penetration, radial explosions, ammo feeds/overheat, charge tiers, attachment stacking and ballistic aim/lead solving
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md for exact coverage and authority boundaries. Policies do not automatically replace existing engine movement/combat/victory or wire presentation. Persist versioned state and bind immutable definitions. Use actual native/host owners for commands, collision and damage. 0.2.0 adds genre/Ballistics.h (penetration, explosions, launch/intercept solver), genre/WeaponMods.h (ammo feeds, charge modes, attachments), genre/WeaponData.h (settings adapters and weapons JSON) and genre/WeaponPersistence.h (save/load kinds 16-18 and hashing); Weapons.h API is unchanged. Built-in FPS ammo/reload stays authoritative.

packages.summary: Deterministic genre bot policies: melee spacing/attack timing/dodge-parry/lock-on, shooter aim/lead/burst/reload/overheat/cover, squad roles with formations and an objective choice hook
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (action-bots) for exact coverage. Bots return player-equivalent inputs (MeleeInput, ShooterInput, role orders, objective choice) for the owner's ordinary command path and never write state. Perception is owner-supplied and must be visibility-authorized. Owner RNG only; repeated/backwards ticks rejected. Persist MeleeBotState/ShooterBotState/SquadState via genre::save/load (record kinds 56-58, 59-63 reserved) and hash them with genreBotHash. bots/SensesPerception.h (perceivedFromSenses) turns stealth-senses PerceivedTarget records into bot input: visible+Alert targets are engageable with owner facts, Searching targets are remembered at lastKnown.

packages.summary: Delta compression of authoritative snapshots for any game: stable record IDs, removed / new / changed records, XOR runs against an acknowledged baseline, per-peer sender history and receiver history over lossy latest-only channels
packages.notes: Host-side networking, not simulation. The server converts its snapshot to a RecordSet (0 = globals, kind bits | entity id), DeltaSender::encode per peer with increasing sequences, acknowledge() from the client's ack (FPS: input viewTick); DeltaReceiver::decode on the client. Lost packets fall back to older acknowledged baselines or a full snapshot. Decoding is bounded and rejects malformed or unknown-baseline packets; validate the rebuilt snapshot as before. Used by the FPS authority session (protocol 5). No encryption, reliability or bandwidth scheduling.

packages.summary: Deterministic kinematic physical interactions: pick up/carry (hold point, mass limit, speed penalty, drop when blocked), charged throws with arc preview from the same integrator and swept landing, push/pull on a grid or free with friction/mass resistance and blocking, XPBD ropes/joints with a fixed iteration count, attach/detach and breaking force, hinged/sliding doors with locks, keys, one-way rules, timing and auto-reverse, waypoint moving platforms with per-rider carry deltas, breakable objects with damage types, thresholds, stages and debris requests
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (physical-interactions) for exact coverage, the determinism/network model and authority boundaries. These Fixed/integer-tick policies are the authoritative state; collision comes from the owner (WorldCollision adapts engine/world SpatialWorld). Box3D (engine/physics) is presentation-only here: it may simulate debris from DebrisRequest but is never read back. Outputs are state + InteractionEvents/requests; no rendering. Repeated/backwards ticks and invalid input return nullopt with state untouched. Platform carry deltas feed the rider position before LocomotionModes runs. Persist CarryState/PushState/RopeState/DoorState/PlatformState/BreakableState via genre::save/load (record kinds 80..87 reserved, 80..85 used), hash with interactionHash, bind interactionConfigHash and interactionDefinitionsHash. packages.summary: Deterministic kinematic vehicle controllers: wheeled arcade-sim (torque curve, auto/manual gears with shift time, per-wheel traction with slip/grip curves, weight transfer, handbrake, drift), tracked differential steering, hover altitude hold with drift damping, arcade flight with banked turns and stall; damage zones with per-zone performance penalties and critical disable; driver/passenger/gunner seats with validated enter/exit/switch/eject and owner-checked exit points; ordered checkpoints, laps, race positions, wrong-way detection and respawn at the last checkpoint; race bot (racing line, corner braking, overtaking lanes, rubber band); race session from grid to results (countdown, bot/player pedals, phases, finish grace, timeout, winner)
packages.notes: Read docs/mechanics-packages.md (vehicle-controllers) for the determinism/network model. The controllers are the authoritative Fixed/integer state: the owner reports ground/wheel contacts (VehicleContacts) and resolves collisions after the step with vehicleResolveCollision; no physics backend is authoritative (Box3D may only mirror poses). stepVehicle/stepVehicleDamage/stepVehicleSeats/stepRace once per strictly increasing tick; invalid input returns nullopt with state untouched. Checkpoints reuse match-rules route gates (RouteGate, crossesGate, stepRoute). mechanics/VehicleDrive.h is the one controls -> pedals mapping of every host (axes; screen stick tank / steer). bots/RaceBot.h returns a VehicleInput like a player. mechanics/RaceSession.h runs a whole race for any host: raceSessionInputs before the vehicles step, stepRaceSession after the collisions (any project: rules and map "race", docs/races.md; adapters in the FPS and driving hosts); mechanics/RaceSessionData.h reads the shared race data. Persist VehicleState 88, VehicleDamageState 89, VehicleSeatState 90, RaceState 91, RaceBotState 94, RaceSessionState 128 via genre::save/load (88..95 shared with sports-rules); hash with vehicleHash and bind vehicleDefinitionHash/raceCourseHash/raceLineHash. Optional `vehicles` settings section. Executable example: examples/libraries/mechanics/vehicles-sports (4-car race). No rendering, audio, suspension geometry or tyre thermal model.

packages.summary: Deterministic ball-sport rules: possession with pickup radius and possession lock, tackles contested with the passed RNG, passes with receiver leading and shots with power and seeded accuracy error, interception at the closest approach along the ball path, goals, out of bounds and generic restarts (kickoff, throw-in, corner, goal kick, free kick, penalty, face-off), walls/rebound fields, periods with running/stopped/added-stoppage clocks and golden-goal overtime, fouls from contact rules; role-based formations with stable slot assignment; positioning bot (formation slots, press/mark/chase, keeper line, pass/shot choice)

Field frame Vec2{x length, y width}, team index 0 attacks +x in odd periods (swapEnds). Persist SportsState 92 and SportsBotState 95 via genre::save/load (93 reserved; 88..95 shared with vehicle-controllers) together with the RNG state; hash with sportsHash and bind sportsDefinitionsHash. packages.summary: Game clock from simulation ticks: day / minute / weekday, inverse tick lookup, work shifts over midnight, fixed and rotating (staggered) work weeks, minutes until the next shift, waking hours with rest after night shifts, needs as time since last met (per-mille urgency, most urgent pick), seeded daily errands with per-day and concurrent caps
packages.notes: Integers only; every query is a pure function of the tick and saved values. Persist only satisfied minutes and DailyErrands (NativeState). planDailyErrands draws in population order with the simulation RNG (below/range) once per day; call markStarted only for errands really started, markSkipped for those given up. minutesUntilShift returns -1 when nobody works within the horizon. Not a scheduler of entities: the owner moves people.

packages.summary: Presentation weather as a pure function of simulation time: seeded showers and wind gusts per time slot with fade envelopes, wet ground and puddles that soak and dry, optional wet opening, shower chance, day phase for the sky
packages.notes: double/float presentation only: never feed back into simulation (gameplay weather is the map environment, docs/game-format.md). No state, so pause / seek / restore need no cache. Default config reproduces the city sample game formula exactly (test). Drive shader wetness, rain particles, wind sway and sound from the sample.

packages.summary: Vehicle look helpers: lamp channels by model part name (headlight, tail, brake with hold after hard deceleration, reverse, indicators / hazards blink, beacon double-flash strobe left/right out of phase, roof sign, destination board) and tyre marks (slip detection, bounded fading trail segments per wheel, wheel contact points)
packages.notes: Presentation only, float, no renderer dependency: the client samples simulation state each frame and draws emissive levels / trail quads itself. TyreTrails keeps an ordered wheel map; call keepOnly with the wheels sampled this frame. Lamp levels are 0/1; smooth them in the view if wanted.

packages.summary: Fixed-point swept tests: circle versus moving oriented box with entry/exit window (pedestrian crossing danger), axis-aligned box slide of short walker moves (walls, furniture), conservative polyline bounds broad phase
packages.notes: Fixed only, no state. Grow boxes by the walker radius with inflate before slideMove; slideMove clamps x first, then z. polylineBounds of an empty line is invalid and touches everything (a broad phase never rejects what it cannot judge). Exact narrow-phase tests stay with the owner.

packages.summary: Caches for derived lookups of native modules: per-id key strings "<prefix><id><suffix>" (dense and bounded sparse) and per-id node pointers into string-keyed maps invalidated by the map erase/insert counters
packages.notes: Never saved, hashed or rolled back; results must equal a plain lookup. NodeCache only for node-based maps exposing erasures()/inserts(); a load or rebuild must bump erasures. One cache per thread/owner (thread_local is fine). SparseKeys uses an unordered map for lookups only, never iterated.

packages.summary: City traffic kernels: road network from a cell mask or curved spline pieces, lanes, junction turns, signal phases and pedestrian walk windows, bot driver pedals, sidewalk walker paths; routes for large/emergency vehicles (wide-street exit choice, bounded local detour around a blockage)
packages.notes: Header kernels used by engine/game/Traffic (rules traffic, docs/traffic.md) and usable from a native module without the RTS module. Fixed / integers and the immutable net only. trafficWideExit always allows the first and the last piece so stations on narrow streets stay reachable; trafficLocalDetour is bounded by its lattice and must be followed by the normal collision checks.

packages.summary: Python tools for split rules.json: compose includes like the engine, write every top-level key and member back to the file it came from, path-like rules_file for old scripts, and split_rules that cuts rules.json into topic and type files by a per-game plan without changing the composed document
packages.notes: Import scripts and installers read and write rules only through rules_io.load/save or rules_io.rules_file; open() on rules.json sees only the root file. split_rules keeps the order of types (part of a game), asserts the composed document is unchanged, and reads <project>/rules-split.json (ownFile, typeLimitKB, prefixes). C++ readers use readComposedJson (engine/data/JsonCompose.h).

packages.summary: Mutable block world for Minecraft-like games: 16^3 chunks with block ids, metadata and derived light; block definitions from JSON (shapes, layers, opacity, emission, drops, fluids, falling, growth, textures); simulated edits with chunk revisions and an edit log; parking of edited chunks on unload; canonical palette+RLE chunk codec and checksummed region files; Fixed ray to the first block and axis-separated box movement against solid blocks; NativeState save record 120
packages.notes: Read docs/voxel.md. Simulation layer, integers and Fixed only, std::map order. Untouched chunks are regenerated from the seed, edited chunks are saved (resident) or parked (unloaded); after loadVoxelWorld the host makes the same chunks resident again before the next tick and then hash() matches. Light is derived: never hashed or saved. Unloaded chunks are solid for queries. Stream whole columns (voxel-light). Record kind 120 (120..127 reserved for voxel packages).

packages.summary: Sky and block light 0..15 for voxel worlds by breadth-first flood fill: straight full-strength sky columns, sideways loss by opacity, emitters, incremental removal and refill after each block edit, columns shaded by chunks loaded above, light level queries for spawning and growth
packages.notes: Deterministic (FIFO queues, fixed neighbour order) but derived: recompute after load with lightChunk / lightPending, then relightBlock(pos, oldBlock) after every VoxelWorld::set. Incremental result equals a full recompute (tested). Marks meshes that sample changed light dirty. Load whole columns so sky light is right. Measured on a dev VM: 0.33 ms per generated chunk, about 3 us per edit.

packages.summary: CPU chunk meshes for voxel worlds: hidden-face culling, greedy merging of equal faces, per-vertex ambient occlusion with anisotropy-safe diagonals, smooth sky/block light, opaque/cutout/translucent layers, cross plants with facing normals, fluids lowered by level, upright side textures in block UVs, back-to-front translucent sort; copyable 18^3 input for worker threads
packages.notes: Presentation only (floats). Build VoxelMeshInput on the owner thread, mesh anywhere, upload on the render thread. Positions are chunk-local: add the chunk origin relative to the camera origin in Fixed before converting (engine/world relativeTo). UVs are in blocks: texture arrays with repeat or fract() in the shader. Unloaded neighbours count as opaque by default. 0.11 ms per chunk average on a dev VM; vertex format is 28 bytes, not packed yet.

packages.summary: Deterministic per-chunk generator for infinite voxel worlds: integer value noise with fractal octaves for height, biomes by temperature noise (surface, filler, shore, height offset), 3D worm caves, ore veins as random walks, trees and plants, bedrock and sea; border-crossing features from per-origin random streams so any generation order gives identical chunks; JSON config by block names
packages.notes: Only integers and engine Random. A golden hash in tests/libraries/voxel_tests.cpp pins the output: change it only on purpose and note it in docs/voxel.md. Structures (villages, dungeons) are not generated yet (capability-status W3). 0.2 ms per chunk on a dev VM.

packages.summary: Scheduled block updates for voxel worlds: flowing fluids with levels and falling columns, infinite sources, draining, fluid reactions (lava + water -> obsidian / cobblestone), falling blocks, random ticks for growth; deterministic queue (due tick, sequence), bounded updates per step, changes reported with old blocks for relighting; NativeState save record 121
packages.notes: Call notifyVoxelChange after every edit of the host (player digging, placing); stepVoxelTicks once per strictly increasing tick with the simulation Random; relight every reported change. Pass the set of active chunks to limit random ticks. Redstone-like logic is not included.

packages.summary: Mob navigation in mutable voxel worlds: A* over feet cells with step-up, bounded drops, swimming and optional diagonals without corner cutting, integer costs and positional ties, node budget; spawn spot search by light level (with night sky darkening), ground blocks and distance
packages.notes: No prebuilt mesh: every query sees the current blocks, so edits need no rebuild. Bound maxNodes per query and spread queries over ticks; cache paths and re-plan when a block on the path changes. Light comes from voxel-light. Measured: 52-step path over generated terrain in 22 ms with 20000 nodes on a dev VM - budget it.

packages.summary: Server-authoritative streaming of voxel worlds: per-client view (radius, vertical range), nearest-first chunk snapshots within byte and chunk budgets, unload notices, compact edit batches by chunk revision, automatic full resend on revision gaps or edit overflow, canonical message bytes and a client mirror that applies them
packages.notes: Host side only, never inside simulation ticks. Use with an authoritative server (engine/net authority or city server style), not lockstep. Send over a reliable ordered channel; drain VoxelWorld::edits after pumping every peer. The mirror needs voxel-light for inserted chunks and applied edits. Delta compression of snapshots is not added.

packages.summary: Shared deterministic hitscan candidate ray intersection with eligibility, immutable rewind poses and nearest-hit tie consistency for FPS, RTS and native games
packages.notes: Live FPS traceShot uses this policy over lag-compensated CharacterSnapshot rewind frames. The policy chooses nearest candidate only; environment/vehicle obstruction and downstream damage remain host-specific. C++ native builds and replay parity remain unverified.

packages.summary: Independent reusable ECS hitscan resolution system: one-shot intents, deterministic nearest-target callbacks, stable hit records and deferred hit application for native games
packages.notes: The real FPS traceShot still uses synchronous shared closest-target and ordered-impact policies; this newly schedulable stage is opt-in only until multi-hit same-tick damage and save/rollback parity have been proven. Does not simulate projectile physics.

packages.summary: Genre-independent ordered ECS projectile impact dispatch for direct damage, queued on-hit effects and splash candidates with injected faction, armor and damage policies
packages.notes: Live ordinary RTS weapon projectiles use this shared policy. It is a synchronous policy inside the existing RTS ECS tick, not a separate scheduled damage stage; FPS and RTS ability adapters remain pending.

packages.summary: Shared nonphysical ECS projectiles with deterministic fixed-tick endpoint arrival or moving-target pursuit; canonical arrival events and deferred despawn
packages.notes: Header-only motion without SpatialWorld or ballistics. Real RTS uses the common pursuit policy but still owns legacy damage/effect ordering. Full RTS migration and native build parity remain pending.

packages.summary: Genre-independent ECS projectile motion/impact assembly: shared flight components, deterministic ballistic or injected guidance policy, read-only collision provider, ordered hit records and deferred despawn
packages.notes: Opt-in composable flight/impact stage only, NOT full FPS/RTS combat migration. Bind separate weapon launch, damage/status and presentation systems; no genre module dependencies. Run cross-genre CTest and native builds before production enablement.

packages.summary: Genre-independent ECS projectile-impact to damage resolution: health/damage components, collider-entity mapping, ordered damage queue, configurable damage policy and applied-event callback
packages.notes: Composable impact/damage stage. Shared with any shooter, artillery, vehicle or spell host. Does not automatically replace legacy FPS/RTS combat logic. Native C++/COW/rollback verification pending.

packages.summary: Universal ECS fire intent, weapon ammo/cooldown, deterministic deferred projectile creation, integrated with shared ballistic flight and impact/damage pipeline
packages.notes: Reusable weapon launch/shot composition for any genre or native host. Legacy FPS/RTS weapon systems still require parity-checked migration; does not claim complete replacement. Native/CI tests pending.

packages.summary: Reusable ECS weapon reload/fire gating, hit-point and energy regeneration, and deterministic entity expiration systems for any genre.
packages.notes: Opt-in native mechanics. Reuses shared ECS weapon/health states, no FPS/RTS dependency. Built-in FPS/RTS authority integration, native CTest and serialization/network parity still pending.

packages.summary: Reusable ECS movement input/state/output components over the existing deterministic stepMotion character locomotion policy, with jump edges and rollback.
packages.notes: Independent movement policy only. Collision, position integration, advanced mode machine and FPS/RTS authority migration remain separate. Native compile/CTest not yet verified.

packages.summary: Genre-independent authoritative ECS inventory item add/remove/transfer transactions with deterministic request IDs, capacity/weight checks and ordered outcomes.
packages.notes: Uses existing gameplay Inventory policies. Permission/faction/distance checks belong to validated host Commands. Built-in FPS/RTS bag integration and native tests remain pending.

packages.summary: Composable ECS ordered impact resolution stage with bounded rollback-owned request queue, stable sequence IDs and host-injected direct/on-hit/splash policies
packages.notes: Opt-in separately scheduled impact barrier. Callback-submitted requests execute on next invocation. Existing RTS immediate per-projectile damage and FPS hit paths must not be switched until real save/checksum/rollback parity is proven.

packages.summary: NEREID deterministic fixed-point ECS water volume sampling across game genres
packages.notes: Stages 1-6: fixed-point bodies/probes, polygon/spline footprints, indexed/adaptive sampling, optional native setup and read-only legacy raster import. Legacy RTS/editor remains authoritative; no production runtime or water rendering adoption. Native tests unverified.

packages.summary: NEREID shared deterministic buoyancy and flow drag output for host physics
packages.notes: Stage 2 policy only; host owns gravity, canonical velocity, collision and force integration. Requires same-tick contact sample. Sphere seas (planets): NereidSphereWater.h, radial sampling/buoyancy/current, test ecs_nereid_sphere_water_test.

packages.summary: NEREID deterministic ECS entry/exit/wake events with ordered read-only VFX/audio presentation snapshots
packages.notes: Optional native pipeline stage after same-tick water contact sampling; outputs are single-tick events, host owns physics and VFX/audio playback. Native execution has not been verified.

packages.summary: NEREID genre-independent waterfall/cascade ECS geometry, persistence and visual ribbon mesh
packages.notes: Stage 27: opt-in descending cascade components, double-sided CPU ribbons and WorldScene graphics; host owns terrain, physics and particle effects. Build/GPU tests deferred by owner.

packages.summary: NEREID fixed-point per-river spatial flow field with downstream, lateral and shear currents
packages.notes: Optional NEREID WaterCurrentFieldComponent: one profile node per RiverSpline point; reference and indexed ECS sampling share deterministic flow. Build/tests deferred.

packages.summary: NEREID deterministic bounded vortex/eddy currents for water contacts and visuals
packages.notes: Optional per-water body WaterVortexFieldComponent, fixed-point additive swirl and radial current with shared reference/indexed sampling. Tests deferred.

packages.summary: Third-person camera boom: orbit, shoulder offset and swap, obstacle avoidance by owner sphere sweep, recenter behind the target, profile stack with blends
packages.notes: Capability P2. LENS (engine/render/CameraBehavior.h, docs/camera-behaviors.md) owns view cameras: register this boom as a LENS body (`shoulder`) and an ECS rig mode before using it in a game - not done yet. No collision with moving bodies unless the sweep reports them. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Off-mesh navigation links (jump, drop, ladder, climb, door, teleport) planned together with any walking mesh, link traversal over ticks, cover spot generation from boxes
packages.notes: Capability F2. Links are not extracted from geometry automatically; the planner calls meshCost for node pairs (fine for hundreds of links). Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: 3D navigation for flyers, ships and swimmers: occupancy grid from boxes, deterministic 26-neighbour A* with smoothing, flock avoidance and 3D formation slots
packages.notes: Capability R5. Dense grid (up to 4M cells); no hierarchical or streamed volumes yet. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Destructible structures of box pieces: area damage, fracture into fragments, support graph collapse, authoritative debris and dirty regions for collision/navmesh/visibility
packages.notes: Capability F3. Box pieces only (no arbitrary mesh slicing); support is connectivity, not stress analysis; no soft bodies. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Linked portals with position/velocity/facing transfer and recursive view transforms, plus gameplay time rewind over a bounded snapshot history with an energy budget
packages.notes: Capability Q4. No portal-in-portal physics for bodies larger than the opening; rewind of single objects (local time bubbles) is left to the owner. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Seeded item generation with prefix/suffix affix pools, tiers, groups and item level, crafting rerolls, coloured sockets and gems, elemental auras and reactions, item migration
packages.notes: Capability A2. No UI; affix text and balance are content. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Quests as data: stages, counted and optional objectives, branches, prerequisites, time limits, abandon/fail/repeat, tracked quest, bounded journal and versioned migration
packages.notes: Capability A4. No quest UI widgets yet; journal text is content. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Wounds by type and body part with bleeding, pain, healing, infection and treatments; diseases with incubation, symptoms, contagion, cures and immunity
packages.notes: Capability S1. No per-limb loss of function; medical UI is not included. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Herds with leader, cohesion, spreading panic and succession, off-screen aggregate herds, and taming by trust with follow/stay/guard orders
packages.notes: Capability S2. No breeding of tamed animals or saddles/riding. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Colonist families, memories with decay and stacking, opinions, friendships and rivalries with hysteresis, partnerships, item ownership and social mood
packages.notes: Capability C1. Births and ageing belong to the owner; no conversation generator. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Pressure-driven pipe networks with sources, sinks, tanks, pumps and valves, and heat exchange between rooms with doors, outdoor boundary and thermostats
packages.notes: Capability C2. Pressure is a relaxed approximation, not a hydraulic solver; no gas mixing. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Trains on a track graph with block signalling, acceleration and braking, looping routes and station stops with dwell times
packages.notes: Capability C2. No junction pathfinding (routes are explicit), no chain signals, no train length. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: City economy and politics: zoned lots that grow by demand, residents and jobs, taxes, service coverage, budget with loans, policies, faction approval and elections
packages.notes: Capability C3. Aggregated lots (no individual citizens); land value is data the owner sets. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Public transport and freight lines with timetables, earliest-arrival route planning with transfers, boarding by capacity and stop congestion diagnostics
packages.notes: Capability C4. Vehicles are timetable entities (the owner moves bodies along roads/rails); no fares. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Multi-storey tactical boards: stacked tactics-grid levels with stairs and ladders, movement across levels, sight through open floors, height advantage and undoable move plans
packages.notes: Capability T2. Destructible floors are left to structure-destruction plus a board rebuild. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Relations from decaying modifiers, treaties with truce and break penalties, defensive alliances that join wars, deal evaluation and a strategy advisor for AI factions
packages.notes: Capability T3. No espionage or vassal tribute flows; the economic value of items comes from the owner. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Generic game-tree search for any turn rules: iterative-deepening alpha-beta with a node budget and seeded MCTS, both explaining the chosen move
packages.notes: Capability T4. Two-sided games; hidden information needs determinization by the owner (see card-games CardBot). Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Hero match rules: pick/ban draft with timeouts, in-match shop with recipes, sell-back and courier delivery, recall channel, last hits, denies, assists, bounties and respawn timers
packages.notes: Capability M1. Lanes, creeps and towers are ordinary units of the host; no MMR here (see meta-matchmaking). Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Boats and ships from assembled hull blocks with point buoyancy, water drag, thrust and rudder, capsize and sinking, plus an aircraft model with lift, drag, stall and control surfaces
packages.notes: Capability V2. Simplified rigid model (no wave slamming, no propeller wash); multi-seat network play is not verified here. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Hidden information for authoritative servers: zones with visibility rules, per-seat opaque handles re-keyed on shuffle, reveal events, reconnect snapshots and commit/reveal rounds
packages.notes: Capability K2. Transport and encryption belong to engine/net; the default FNV commitment is not cryptographic. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Lip-sync viseme tracks from recorded speech (loudness, zero crossings, band energy, closed-lip gaps) or from text, with attack/release smoothing and sampling for the face rig
packages.notes: Capability A3. Energy/spectral heuristics, not a phoneme recogniser; Latin text only. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Touch controls (fixed and floating sticks, hold/toggle buttons, tap, double tap, long press, swipe, pinch, rotate, pan) and accessibility settings (colour vision, scales, subtitles, reduced motion, remapping with conflicts)
packages.notes: Capability U1. No on-screen widgets (draw them with the UI layer); colour compensation is per colour, not a post-process pass. Tests: tests/libraries/policy_mechanics_tests.cpp.

packages.summary: Planar geometry, triangulation, Voronoi, 3D ray and primitive distance/overlap queries
packages.notes: Coordinate bound ±1e9; no render dependencies.

packages.summary: Portable RNG, weighted sampling, distributions, low discrepancy and spatial sampling
packages.notes: Explicit state; no replacement of simulation RNG.

packages.summary: Deterministic scalar, simplex, cellular, fractal, vector, warp, curl and batch noise
packages.notes: Fixed-point scalar kernels and composition; NoiseBatch.h provides allocation-free AoS/SoA input sampling with typed outputs, atomic or validity-mask policy. Legacy GenNoise unchanged.
